requirements.requirement: A containerized web application runs on node1 as the unprivileged appsvc account and serves on port 8080.
requirements.summary: The HTTP process runs as appsvc UID/GID 999, maps container UID 0 only to host UID 999, has distinct user, mount, UTS, IPC, and PID namespaces with NSpid 1, listens on port 8080, and returns the expected content. The same behavior is directly shown before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The application starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session.
requirements.summary: Linger is enabled, Sessions and Display are empty, and the appsvc user manager and web service are active. A scheduled restart produced a different boot identity, after which the user manager, namespaced application, listener, and HTTP content recovered without an appsvc login session.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The node-restart protocol is strong: it captures a healthy pre-restart service and boot identity, restart scheduling and temporary SSH unavailability, a changed post-restart boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, content, account/session, and namespace state.
limitations: The fixed after-executor listening-sockets observation is empty despite the immediately preceding direct command showing an active :::8080 listener and successful HTTP response. Because the lifecycle socket observation was also empty at baseline despite active SSH access, its socket coverage appears limited, but the discrepancy prevents maximum confidence.
There is no cluster state to assess because the managed topology contains only one standalone node.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The persistent changes in cmd-b027f9e2d9bb40c8 created the required account, root filesystem, launcher, content, and user unit; cmd-977360e10c5c422c enabled lingering and started the necessary user manager; cmd-aa5089ade84f4f27 scheduled the required bounded restart test. The remaining commands were discovery, verification, or read-only restart polling. No failed services, package damage, or executor-created temporary residue was observed after execution.
